title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is manuscript p. 746 of the continuation of La Longue Marche (1981). The previous page set up the universal case (13): 1 → Π̂_{g,ν} → M_{g,ν} = π1(universal curve over Q) → N_{g,ν} = π1(M_{g,ν,Q}) → 1. Grothendieck wants an abstract, axiomatic property shared by this universal case and by the case of a curve over a field k finitely generated over Q. The universal case reduces to the second by passing to the generic point of M_{g,ν}.

On this page he fixes the abstract set-up.
- M is a 'Π-group' (profinite) with a distinguished normal 'subgroup of definition' Π. Π is then a profinite 'groupe à lacets': a profinite surface group with its structure of cusp-loop (inertia) subgroups.
- This gives the exact sequence (14): 1 → Π → M → N → 1.
- A 'tore' is an embedding (15) K: T ↪ Π, where T ≅ Ẑ(1) is the standard pro-cyclic 'torus'. K must be compatible with the lacets structure of Π, so its image L = K(T) is a cuspidal inertia subgroup.
- He takes the normalizer (16) N(L) = Norm_M(L) and considers the conjugation action of N(L)/L on L. Writing N(L)/L ⊂ N tacitly uses that N(L) ∩ Π = L, i.e. cuspidal inertia subgroups are self-normalizing in the profinite surface group.
- NB: the image of N(L)/L in N is open. Reason: N acts on the finitely many Π-conjugacy classes of loop subgroups, so the stabilizer of the class of L is open, and N(L) surjects onto it.
- Since Aut(L) = Ẑ*, the action is a character. He asserts it is the restriction of a 'cyclotomic character' χ_N: N → Ẑ* (17), which on the next page he says is intrinsic to M, written χ_M (18).
- Essential hypothesis (next page): Im(χ_N) is open in Ẑ*. This holds over any field finitely generated over Q.
- Consequence (19): every open subgroup of N(L)/L acts non-trivially on L.
- He then appeals to 'standard arguments'. The aim is presumably a group-theoretic, weight-type rigidity for the extension: centralizers, characterization of the tores/loops, and faithfulness or injectivity of the outer action.

In modern terms, he is axiomatizing an 'arithmetic profinite surface-group extension with cyclotomically acting cusps'. This is the framework later used in anabelian geometry, e.g. Nakamura's characterization of cuspidal inertia subgroups via the cyclotomic character, and Mochizuki's work.
errors: The text tacitly uses N(L) ∩ Π = L (self-normalizing cusp subgroups) when writing N(L)/L ⊂ N. This is true for hyperbolic profinite surface groups but is not stated or proved here.
That the action on L is via χ_N (the same cyclotomic character for all cusps) is asserted, not justified, in the abstract axiomatic setting. It holds in the geometric situation.

ideas.what: Abstract axiomatic framework: profinite extension 1→Π→M→N→1 with Π a profinite surface group 'à lacets', M a 'Π-group' with intrinsic cyclotomic character
ideas.modern_name: arithmetic profinite (outer) Galois representation on a profinite surface group; abstract 'Galois-type' extensions in anabelian geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Longue Marche/Esquisse); developed by Nakamura, Tamagawa, Mochizuki in the 1990s
ideas.where_published: Ideas present in La Longue Marche (1981) and the letter to Faltings (1983); this specific continuation is unpublished as far as I know

ideas.what: Cuspidal inertia ('tore'/'lacet') subgroup L ≅ Ẑ(1), its normalizer, and the action of N(L)/L on L via the cyclotomic character; openness of the image in N
ideas.modern_name: decomposition/inertia groups of cusps; cyclotomic action on cuspidal inertia
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (SGA1 tame fundamental group theory); group-theoretic use by Nakamura (1990) and Mochizuki
ideas.where_published: Tame inertia is Ẑ(1) in SGA 1 / Grothendieck–Murre; this normalizer argument is not published as far as I know

ideas.what: Hypothesis that the cyclotomic character has open image, giving: every open subgroup of N(L)/L acts non-trivially on L
ideas.modern_name: open-image cyclotomic hypothesis / weight argument (no open subgroup fixing Ẑ(1))
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard; used systematically in anabelian proofs (Nakamura, Tamagawa, Mochizuki)

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates an intrinsic axiomatic setting in which the cyclotomic character on M, together with the open-image hypothesis, is to be used to recover the loop/torus structure and rigidity group-theoretically. This anticipates the later group-theoretic characterization of cuspidal inertia subgroups via cyclotomic weights (Nakamura 1990; Mochizuki's 'cuspidalization' and abstract absolute anabelian frameworks).
missed.quote: Cette action se fait par un "caractère cyclotomique", induit par un caractère N →χ_N Ẑ*. L'hypothèse essentielle est que l'image ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority: it shows Grothendieck himself began axiomatizing 'Π-groups with cyclotomic character' as abstract objects, which is close in spirit to Mochizuki's abstract treatment. It is of moderate interest for the history of anabelian geometry, not mathematically new.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard (cusp inertia, normalizers, cyclotomic action with open image). The interest is historical: an unpublished, explicit axiomatization of arithmetic surface-group extensions with an intrinsic cyclotomic character, prefiguring 1990s anabelian group-theoretic methods.
transcription_corrections: Line 2–3: 'qui sera donc un groupe profini' is likely 'qui sera donc un groupe à lacets' (followed by a crossed-out word); Π carries a 'lacets' (cusp-loop) structure.
'relatif : la structure profinie de Π' should probably read 'relatif à la structure à lacets de Π' (or 'relatif : la structure à lacets de Π').
'et un tore [?]' — the word 'tore' seems right ('et un tore').
'considérons l'action de N(L)/L ⊂ N dans L' — the image reads roughly 'dans ce L'.
'est un sous-groupe ouvert de N' — 'ouvert' is a superscript insertion.
